questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a constituent component of a nucleotide? (FBISE 2024-II, Official Test Series)
questions.explanation: A nucleotide is composed of three building blocks: a nitrogenous base, a five-carbon pentose sugar, and a phosphate group. Amino acids are the building blocks of proteins, not nucleotides.

questions.question: What nitrogenous base is present in RNA but absent in DNA? (FBISE 2023-II, Official Test Series)
questions.explanation: RNA contains the pyrimidine base uracil ($U$) instead of thymine ($T$), which is found exclusively in DNA.

questions.question: Which fat-soluble vitamin plays a crucial role in blood clotting? (FBISE 2022-I, Official Test Series)
questions.explanation: Vitamin K is essential for the liver synthesis of prothrombin and other blood clotting factors; its deficiency results in delayed blood coagulation and hemorrhagic disorders.

questions.question: A deficiency of Vitamin D in growing children leads to the bone disease: (FBISE 2021-I, Official Test Series)
questions.explanation: Vitamin D promotes intestinal calcium and phosphate absorption. In children, Vitamin D deficiency leads to rickets, characterized by soft, weak, and deformed bones.

questions.question: Which vitamin is essential for maintaining healthy vision and the synthesis of visual purple (rhodopsin)? (FBISE 2020-II, Official Test Series)
questions.explanation: Vitamin A (retinol) is an essential component of rhodopsin, the light-sensitive pigment in retinal rod cells. Deficiency causes night blindness (nyctalopia) and xerophthalmia.

questions.question: Which of the following is classified as a water-soluble vitamin? (FBISE 2019-I, Official Test Series)
questions.explanation: Vitamins B-complex and C are water-soluble vitamins that are not stored in significant quantities in the human body and must be regularly supplied in the daily diet.

questions.question: Proteins are biopolymers constructed from repeating units of: (FBISE 2018-II, Official Test Series)
questions.explanation: Proteins are long macromolecular polymers of $\alpha$-amino acids linked together in a specific sequence by covalent peptide bonds ($-CO-NH-$).

questions.question: The covalent linkage formed between the amino group of one amino acid and the carboxyl group of another is called a: (FBISE 2017-I, 2023-I)
questions.explanation: During protein synthesis, a condensation reaction between $-COOH$ of one amino acid and $-NH_2$ of another eliminates a water molecule, creating an amide/peptide linkage ($-CO-NH-$).

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a monosaccharide (simple sugar)? (FBISE 2016-II, 2022-II)
questions.explanation: Glucose ($C_6H_{12}O_6$) is an aldohexose monosaccharide that cannot be hydrolyzed into simpler carbohydrate units.

questions.question: Sucrose (cane sugar or table sugar) on hydrolysis yields: (FBISE 2015-I, 2021-II)

options.B: One molecule of glucose and one molecule of fructose
options.C: One molecule of glucose and one molecule of galactose

questions.explanation: Sucrose is a disaccharide consisting of a glucose unit linked to a fructose unit. Acidic or enzymatic hydrolysis cleaves the glycosidic bond into one D-glucose and one D-fructose.

questions.question: Which polysaccharide serves as the main structural component of plant cell walls and makes up 95% of cotton? (FBISE 2014-I, 2020-I)
questions.explanation: Cellulose is an unbranched polymer of $\beta$-D-glucose providing rigidity and tensile strength to plant cell walls. Pure cotton fiber is approximately 95% cellulose.

questions.question: Animal starch, which is stored primarily in the liver and muscles of animals for energy reserve, is: (FBISE 2018-I)
questions.explanation: Glycogen is a highly branched polysaccharide of $\alpha$-D-glucose synthesized in mammals as an internal carbohydrate energy storage reserve, commonly referred to as animal starch.

questions.question: A saturated fatty acid is distinguished by the fact that: (FBISE 2019-II, Official Test Series)

options.B: It contains only single bonds between all carbon atoms in its hydrocarbon chain
options.C: It is always a liquid at room temperature
options.D: It dissolves easily in cold water

questions.explanation: Saturated fatty acids (like palmitic and stearic acids) have no $C=C$ double bonds, meaning all carbon atoms are saturated with hydrogen atoms, typically resulting in solid fats at room temperature.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an unsaturated fatty acid? (FBISE 2017-II)
questions.explanation: Oleic acid contains one cis-double bond ($C=C$) in its 18-carbon chain ($C_{17}H_{33}COOH$), classifying it as a monounsaturated fatty acid found in olive and vegetable oils.

questions.question: Fats and oils are chemically classified as: (FBISE 2016-I, Official Test Series)

options.B: Esters of glycerol and fatty acids (triglycerides)

questions.explanation: Fats and oils are triglycerides—triesters formed from one molecule of the trihydric alcohol glycerol and three long-chain fatty acid molecules.

questions.question: What is the primary biological function of deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA)? (FBISE 2021-I, Official Test Series)

options.B: Storage and transmission of genetic hereditary information
options.C: Transport of oxygen in red blood cells
options.D: Structural support in hair and nails

questions.explanation: DNA contains the master genetic code that instructs cells how to build proteins and transmits hereditary traits from parents to offspring.

questions.question: The primary role of ribonucleic acid (RNA) in cells is: (FBISE 2023-II, Official Test Series)
questions.explanation: RNA molecules (mRNA, tRNA, rRNA) read the genetic instructions stored in DNA and translate them to assemble amino acids into functional proteins.

questions.question: The double helical structure of DNA was discovered in 1953 by: (FBISE 2020-I)

options.B: Robert Hooke and Antonie van Leeuwenhoek

questions.explanation: James Watson and Francis Crick proposed the double helix model of DNA in 1953 based on X-ray diffraction data collected by Rosalind Franklin and Maurice Wilkins.

questions.question: Deficiency of Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) causes: (FBISE 2015-II, Official Test Series)
questions.explanation: Vitamin C is required for collagen hydroxylation. Its deficiency weakens connective tissues, resulting in scurvy, characterized by spongy bleeding gums, skin hemorrhages, and delayed wound healing.

questions.question: Which vitamin functions as a powerful lipid-soluble antioxidant protecting cell membranes from free radical oxidation? (Official Test Series)
questions.explanation: Vitamin E acts as a biological antioxidant, scavenging reactive free radicals and preventing lipid peroxidation in cellular membranes.

questions.question: How many standard amino acids are utilized by living organisms to construct biological proteins? (FBISE 2019-II)
questions.explanation: There are 20 standard $\alpha$-amino acids encoded by the universal genetic code that serve as the universal building blocks for all living proteins.

questions.question: Essential amino acids are defined as those that: (FBISE 2018-II)

options.A: Can be readily synthesized by the human body
options.B: Cannot be synthesized by the human body and must be supplied in food

questions.explanation: Out of 20 amino acids, 10 cannot be synthesized by human metabolic pathways at rates required for health and must be obtained directly through diet; these are termed essential amino acids.

questions.question: Cholesterol belongs to which broad biochemical class of organic compounds? (Official Test Series)
questions.explanation: Cholesterol is a sterol (a modified steroid lipid) derived from animal products that serves as an essential membrane component and precursor for bile acids and steroid hormones.

questions.question: The adipose fat tissue layer situated beneath the skin of mammals primarily acts as: (Official Test Series)

options.B: A thermal insulator preventing heat loss

questions.explanation: Subcutaneous fat has very low thermal conductivity and functions as a biological thermal insulator, conserving body heat in mammals against cold environments.

questions.question: Proteins are essential biological constituents of the living matter of cells known as: (FBISE 2025 Model)
questions.explanation: Protoplasm—the entire living substance of a cell (cytoplasm and nucleus)—consists primarily of water, proteins, nucleic acids, and lipids, where proteins provide structure and enzymatic activity.

questions.question: Which of the following is a pentose sugar found in RNA nucleotides?
questions.explanation: RNA nucleotides contain the five-carbon furanose sugar D-ribose ($C_5H_{10}O_5$), which has a hydroxyl group on carbon-2, unlike 2-deoxyribose in DNA.

questions.question: Which base pairing is complementary in a double-stranded DNA molecule?

options.A: Adenine with Thymine ($A=T$); Guanine with Cytosine ($G\equiv C$)
options.B: Adenine with Guanine; Thymine with Cytosine
options.C: Adenine with Uracil; Guanine with Thymine
options.D: Cytosine with Uracil; Adenine with Thymine

questions.explanation: In DNA, according to Chargaff's rules, Adenine forms two hydrogen bonds with Thymine ($A=T$), and Guanine forms three hydrogen bonds with Cytosine ($G\equiv C$).

questions.question: What type of chemical reaction converts liquid vegetable oils into solid vegetable fats (ghee)?
questions.explanation: Catalytic hydrogenation adds hydrogen across the unsaturated double bonds of liquid oil triglycerides in the presence of nickel at 250°C, transforming them into saturated solid fats.

questions.question: Which carbohydrate gives a characteristic deep blue-black color when treated with iodine solution?
questions.explanation: Starch contains helical amylose coils that trap triiodide ($I_3^-$) ions, forming an intensely colored blue-black coordination complex—the classic diagnostic test for starch.

questions.question: Lactose (milk sugar) is a disaccharide composed of which two monosaccharide units?
questions.explanation: Lactose consists of one molecule of $\beta$-D-galactose linked by a $\beta-(1\to 4)$ glycosidic bond to one molecule of D-glucose.

questions.question: Which of the following is a fibrous, insoluble protein found in human hair, nails, and outer skin layers?
questions.explanation: Keratin is an insoluble, cysteine-rich structural fibrous protein that forms protective outer coverings including hair, fingernails, wool, and feathers.

questions.question: Which globular protein is responsible for transporting oxygen gas in vertebrate red blood cells?
questions.explanation: Hemoglobin is an iron-containing tetrameric globular protein located inside erythrocytes that binds oxygen in the lungs and releases it into body tissues.

questions.question: The primary cause of the neurological condition Beriberi is a severe dietary deficiency of:
questions.explanation: Beriberi results from a deficiency of thiamine (Vitamin B1), which is essential for carbohydrate catabolism and nerve function, common in diets reliant on polished white rice.

questions.question: Which of the following carbohydrates is non-reducing sugar?
questions.explanation: In sucrose, both anomeric carbons of glucose and fructose are bonded together in a $1\to 2$ glycosidic linkage, leaving no free aldehyde or ketone group to reduce Fehling's or Benedict's reagent.

questions.question: What is the general chemical formula representing carbohydrates?
questions.explanation: Carbohydrates were historically considered hydrates of carbon because many have the empirical ratio $C_x(H_2O)_y$ (e.g., glucose is $C_6(H_2O)_6$ or $C_6H_{12}O_6$).

questions.question: Enzymes are specialized biological catalysts composed of:
questions.explanation: All enzymes are globular proteins that speed up biochemical reactions in cells by lowering activation energy while exhibiting exquisite substrate specificity.

questions.question: Which of the following organic acids is a major saturated fatty acid found in butter, palm oil, and animal tallow?
questions.explanation: Palmitic acid is a 16-carbon saturated fatty acid ($CH_3(CH_2)_{14}COOH$) abundantly present in palm oil, dairy fat, and animal adipose tissue.

questions.question: DNA and RNA are composed of alternating chains of:
questions.explanation: The structural backbone of a nucleic acid strand consists of alternating phosphate groups and pentose sugar residues connected by phosphodiester linkages.

questions.question: Fructose is chemically classified as a(n):
questions.explanation: Fructose ($C_6H_{12}O_6$) is a 6-carbon monosaccharide that contains a ketone group at carbon-2, classifying it as a ketohexose (fruit sugar).

questions.question: Which condition is caused by a deficiency of Vitamin B12 (Cobalamin)?
questions.explanation: Vitamin B12 is essential for red blood cell maturation and myelin synthesis. Its deficiency or failure of intrinsic factor absorption produces pernicious (megaloblastic) anemia.

questions.question: Which of the following foods is the richest natural source of Vitamin C?
questions.explanation: Citrus fruits such as oranges, lemons, limes, amla (Indian gooseberry), and guavas are exceptionally rich sources of Vitamin C (ascorbic acid).

questions.question: What type of lipid forms the fundamental lipid bilayer framework of all biological cell membranes?
questions.explanation: Phospholipids have amphipathic properties with a hydrophilic phosphate head and two hydrophobic fatty acid tails, naturally assembling into stable bilayers in aqueous media.

questions.question: Which of the following carbohydrates cannot be digested by the human gastrointestinal tract due to lack of cellulase enzyme?
questions.explanation: Human digestive enzymes can cleave $\alpha-(1\to 4)$ glycosidic bonds in starch, but lack cellulase to hydrolyze $\beta-(1\to 4)$ linkages in cellulose, which passes as insoluble dietary fiber.

questions.question: How many hydrogen bonds connect Guanine and Cytosine in a DNA double helix?
questions.explanation: Between guanine and cytosine, there are three specific hydrogen bonds ($G\equiv C$), providing higher thermal stability than the two hydrogen bonds between adenine and thymine ($A=T$).

questions.question: Which vitamin is synthesized in human skin upon exposure to solar ultraviolet (UV) radiation?
questions.explanation: Photochemical conversion of 7-dehydrocholesterol in the epidermal layer of skin by solar UV-B rays synthesizes cholecalciferol (Vitamin D3).
